top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye is a mature, independently reproduced result in which the magic-wavelength trap is a distinct physical idea (cancelling the light shift so many atoms can be interrogated at once) and not merely a better number. The two-name allocation is clean, with Katori's concept and Ye's many-atom realisation, and the 10^-18 budgets are agreed across several laboratories. The overlap with earlier metrology prizes and the unchecked Sr lattice-clock priority record are real caveats, but they do not outweigh the maturity. Twisted bilayer graphene (P002) is scientifically novel but young, with an unsettled pairing mechanism and an incomplete experimental credit, so it ranks second ahead of no award.
